gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Autel prints the same "recognizing subjects at up to 100m" claim on the 9.1 mm EVO Lite 640T and the 13 mm EVO II Dual 640T V3, although both are sold as "640 × 512" and the 13 mm lens puts about 1.43× as many pixels across the same target.
standout_why: Compared against blog.dronetrader.com/thermal-drones-for-sale, bestthermaldrone.com/best-thermal-drones and /compare, the nighthunting.net/thermal-drones index and its EVO Lite 640T model page. Rivals already hold part of the lens finding: bestthermaldrone lists the 9.1 mm and 13 mm lenses and gives cm-per-pixel for the Matrice 4T (11.5 cm at 400 ft), Mavic 3T (15.6 cm) and Skydio X10, but gives no per-pixel figure for either Autel and says Autel does not publish thermal field of view. nighthunting's Lite 640T page already computes pixels-on-animal from 12 µm and 9.1 mm. None of them puts the two Autel drones side by side or notes the identical 100 m claim. None gives a hover time; DJI's own spec pages do (42 min Matrice 4T, 38 min Mavic 3T). The nine B&H compare pages returned HTTP 403, so I could not check whether they list hover time or thermal focal length; that is why this is 1 and not 2.
decides: It confirms ChatGPT's picks but sharpens the choice between the two Autel drones Dealectric lists. The EVO Lite 640T ($3,359) has the wide 9.1 mm thermal lens, the same focal length nighthunting lists for the discontinued Mavic 3T class: fine for roofs and solar at low height, coarse for spotting animals or people from 400 ft. The EVO II Dual 640T V3 Rugged Bundle ($4,399 at autelpilot.com) buys the 13 mm lens for $1,040 more: about 43% more pixels on the same target and about 30% narrower ground strip. That is narrower than the Matrice 4T's 45° thermal lens as DJI specifies it, so on thermal detail alone the cheaper Autel is not behind the Matrice 4T. Separately, the Matrice 4T's 49-minute lead shrinks to 42 minutes when hovering, which is how inspections and searches are flown.

findings.label: Ground size of one thermal pixel (computed)
findings.value: 13.2 cm at 100 m; 15.8 cm at 120 m (about 400 ft)
findings.note: nighthunting.net lists 640 × 512, 12 µm, 9.1 mm, f/1.0. 12 µm ÷ 9.1 mm = 1.319 mrad per pixel; × 100 m = 13.2 cm. Consistent with nighthunting's own 84 ft strip at 100 ft (640 px). A 0.5 m-wide person at Autel's 100 m spans about 3.8 px. Looking straight down over flat ground.

findings.product: Autel Robotics EVO II Dual 640T V3
findings.label: Ground size of one thermal pixel (computed, assuming 12 µm pitch)
findings.value: 9.2 cm at 100 m; 11.1 cm at 120 m
findings.source_title: EVO II Dual 640T Rugged Bundle V3 (Autel Robotics US store)
findings.note: 12 µm ÷ 13 mm = 0.923 mrad per pixel. The 13 mm is Autel's figure; the 12 µm pitch is an assumption carried over from the Lite and is listed under unsourced. A 0.5 m-wide person at 100 m would span about 5.4 px.
